in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Great! Let me help you check your Child Benefit eligibility. I need to start by understanding your child's situation.

**First question: How old is your child?**

This is important because:
- Children under 16 may automatically qualify
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over generally don't qualify

Could you tell me your child's age?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Let me continue with the assessment based on your situation.

You have Alex, who is 17 years old. Since Alex is between 16-19, I need to check education or extension period eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex currently in approved education or training, or have they recently left education?**

For 16-19 year olds, eligibility depends on their education/training status:
- **In education or training**: If Alex is currently enrolled in approved education or training
- **Recently left education**: If Alex left education within the last 20 weeks (there may be an extension period)
- **Neither**: If Alex is not in education/training and didn't recently leave

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on your situation profile, Alex is 17 years old, not in approved education or extension period, and works 24+ hours per week. Let me continue the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've completed the assessment for your situation. Unfortunately, I need to give you some disappointing news.

## **Eligibility Decision: NOT ELIGIBLE**

**Why you're not eligible:**

Alex is 17 years old, which means they fall into the 16-19 age category. For children in this age group, Child Benefit is only available if they are in approved education or training. Since Alex is not in approved education or training and is working 24+ hours per week, they don't meet the qualifying criteria.

**Important Information:**

- Child Benefit automatically covers children under 16
- For young people aged 16-19, they must be in **approved education or training** to qualify
- Once a child leaves education and is working full-time (24+ hours per week), they are not considered a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes

**What if circumstances change?**

If Alex's situation changes in the future (for example, if they reduce their working hours and enroll in approved education or training), you may become eligible at that point. In such cases, you would need to make a new claim.
